description: When the kidneys are not working well, metformin can build up and raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis.
Ibuprofen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
Naproxen can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and make kidney problems worse.
Simvastatin should not be used in active liver disease because it can further affect the liver.
Liver disease can make paracetamol more likely to cause liver harm.
In older adults, oxybutynin is more likely to cause confusion, constipation and other side effects.
With reduced kidney function, spironolactone can cause high potassium levels.
Children and teenagers are more likely to get movement-related side effects from metoclopramide.
